interpretation_note: Differential playback response does not demonstrate human-like word meaning.
Recruit flights support spatially relevant information use; consider odor and landmarks.
Combinatorial coda structure does not establish compositional semantics.
Gesture exchange timing does not establish shared linguistic conventions.
Different visual displays to different audiences do not establish conscious deception.
Other-species pheromone following may be eavesdropping rather than intended cross-species communication.
Vibration-linked recruitment is demonstrated in sampled nymph groups; do not propagate to entire clade.
Electric organ discharge can serve both electrolocation and social functions.
Spontaneous sighs during sleep are physiological and not inherently communicative.
Sighs associated with relief were not shown to convey safety to another rat.
Context-related horse snorts may function as cues but do not prove emotion or signaling.
Respiratory motor control can alter calls without being its own deliberate signal.
HVC activity correlates with familiarity; behavior and neural sessions differ.
Cortisol or HRV changes are measures of physiology rather than proof of communication.
Tactile grooming solicitation in one group does not establish a species-wide culture.
